note: Friction is per-pair state between two houses that share a land border: the slow accumulation of grievance that the action table alone never produced. Without it the game drifted cooperative — compacts and marriages ran two orders of magnitude ahead of disputes and challenges, because nothing manufactured the Sig− relation that Dispute and then Challenge need. Added as rules version 0.6.
requires: a shared land border between the two houses

opposed_tags.when: one house is Progressive and the other Conservative

either_enclosed.when: either house is enclosed (§7b): a house with nowhere to grow presses on its neighbours

bound.when: a +, ◉+ or kin relation already exists between them; friendship cools a border

decay.when: none of the above applies; grievance fades when nothing feeds it

open_quarrel.when: a Sig− or ⊖ already stands between the pair: friction is unexpressed pressure, and theirs is already expressed, so it neither builds nor decays until the quarrel is settled

flashpoint.note: At the threshold the border is ready to break, but does not have to: a d6 of 4 or more turns friction into a named grievance, and the pair falls back to 30 either way it lands, so a quarrel that does not catch still leaves the border warmer than it started.

grievances.note: The template a flashpoint is named for, chosen by the two houses' tags. Every one of these is a quarrel the 1867-1918 record actually turns on; the engine names the grievance so the chronicle can say what the two houses fell out over.
Progressive|Conservative: the patronage of a shared riding's offices
a church and school dispute in the border townships
Conservative|Conservative: a boundary the two houses read differently
a slighted marriage between the two houses
Progressive|Progressive: the water rights of a shared river
the patronage of a shared riding's offices
Mixed|Mixed: a boundary the two houses read differently
the water rights of a shared river
default: a boundary the two houses read differently
the water rights of a shared river
the patronage of a shared riding's offices
a slighted marriage between the two houses
a church and school dispute in the border townships

contested_expansion.note: §7 never said what happens when two houses reach for the same unclaimed riding in one season. They roll 2d6 against each other; the higher takes it and the loser carries a grievance away. Ties go to the house that drew its action first, which is founding order — the older house has the standing.

correspond_fumble.note: §7 gives Correspond no failure effect at all, which makes it a free action with only upside. A natural 2 — the letter that gives offence — now produces a grievance instead of nothing.

dispute_outcome.note: §7 says a won dispute leaves the grievance 'resolved or ⊖' without saying how often it hardens. PART B assumed half, in code; rules 0.6 moves the number here and tunes it, because it is the tap that feeds Challenge: only a ⊖ makes a challenge legal, so every point of this probability is worth several challenges a run.

grievance_lapse.note: Friction decays when nothing feeds it; a grievance had no such rule, so the map's stock of open Sig− relations only ever grew and every house always had someone to quarrel with. A grievance neither side has acted on for this many seasons lapses to resolved — the quarrel is not settled, it is merely no longer worth pressing. This is the counterpart of per_season.decay and is what holds disputes per house-generation inside the smoke bounds.

challenge_outcome.note: §7 costs a failed challenge ambition and influence but says nothing about the ⊖ that made it legal. Leaving the hostility standing let one pair challenge season after season, which is where the challenge count's seed-to-seed variance came from. A failed challenge now spends the hostility back down to a grievance: the quarrel remains, the moment for arms has passed.
